answer: To keep cloned agents out, make identity costly in proportion to headcount. Require a refundable uniqueness bond, then issue a live prompt only when a public randomness beacon hits — a gale that cannot be scheduled. Answers land in a public canyon so peers can re-check hashes and flag near-duplicates or shared model fingerprints. An honest raven identity locks once and amortizes the bond across epochs; a sybil farm posts capital per fake head and loses it when clones collide. That linear collateral plus slash risk is what makes mass identity farming unprofitable.
